questions.question: According to the course summary of the FlashAttention teaching kernel, what is the core algorithmic idea? [ref_2]
choices: Tiled GEMM + Online Softmax
Sparse attention + pruning
Low-rank approximation of Q and K
Quantizing Q, K and V to INT8
questions.reference_answer: The course states the core algorithmic idea is "Tiled GEMM + Online Softmax" [ref_2]. FlashAttention combines shared-memory tiling of the two GEMMs with an online (streaming) softmax so the full attention matrix never has to be written out.
scoring_points: Selects 'Tiled GEMM + Online Softmax'.
Explains that tiling keeps working set in shared memory / SRAM.
Explains that online softmax lets softmax be computed while streaming over tiles.
knowledge_points: FlashAttention core idea (tiling + online softmax to avoid materializing the attention matrix)

questions.question: Which two intermediate tensors does FlashAttention avoid writing to global memory in full? [ref_2]
choices: S = QK^T and P = softmax(S)
Q and K
V and the output O
The running maximum m and the running normalizer l
questions.reference_answer: The course says FlashAttention avoids "writing the full S = QK^T and P = softmax(S)" [ref_2]. Instead it keeps only running statistics m and l while scanning tiles, so the N x N score and probability matrices are never materialized.
scoring_points: Selects 'S = QK^T and P = softmax(S)'.
Notes that Q, K, V and O must still be stored (they are inputs/outputs).
Notes that m and l are small per-row statistics, not full matrices.
knowledge_points: FlashAttention core idea (tiling + online softmax to avoid materializing the attention matrix)

questions.question: In the FlashAttention loop over key/value tiles, which quantities are carried along as running state? [ref_2]
choices: A running maximum m and a running normalizer l
The full score matrix S
A copy of every previous tile of K
The gradient of the loss with respect to Q
questions.correct_answer: A running maximum m and a running normalizer l
questions.reference_answer: The course describes the kernel as maintaining "running m and l while scanning tiles" [ref_2]. m is the running row maximum used for numerical stability and l is the running sum of exponentials; both are updated incrementally as each tile is processed.
scoring_points: Selects the running maximum m and running normalizer l.
States that m is the running row max used for stability.
States that l is the running sum of exp(x - m).

questions.question: What does the course list as the fused kernel structure that real FlashAttention-1 adds? [ref_2]
choices: QK^T -> online softmax -> PV in one fused kernel
QK^T -> write S to global memory -> separate softmax kernel -> PV
softmax -> QK^T -> PV
PV -> online softmax -> QK^T
questions.correct_answer: QK^T -> online softmax -> PV in one fused kernel
questions.reference_answer: The course lists "One fused kernel: QK^T -> online softmax -> PV" [ref_2]. Fusing the two GEMMs and the softmax into a single kernel is what removes the round trips of S and P through global memory.
scoring_points: Selects the fused QK^T -> online softmax -> PV order.
Explains that fusion avoids global-memory round trips for S and P.
Keeps the correct order: score GEMM, then softmax, then value GEMM.
knowledge_points: FlashAttention core idea (tiling + online softmax to avoid materializing the attention matrix)

questions.question: In the shared-memory tiled GEMM kernel, what is the purpose of the two __syncthreads() calls around the inner compute loop? [ref_17]
choices: The first waits until the whole tile has been loaded into shared memory; the second ensures all threads finish using the tile before the next tile overwrites it
They synchronize the GPU with the host CPU
They allocate the shared-memory arrays As and Bs
They perform the reduction of the sum across threads
questions.correct_answer: The first waits until the whole tile has been loaded into shared memory; the second ensures all threads finish using the tile before the next tile overwrites it
questions.reference_answer: The kernel loads a tile with "// 1. Global Memory => Shared Memory", then has a barrier commented "// Wait until the whole tile has been loaded", computes, and then a second barrier so that all threads finish using this tile before loading the next one [ref_17]. This double-barrier pattern prevents read-after-write and write-after-read races on the shared tiles.
scoring_points: Identifies the first barrier as protecting the tile load (load-before-use).
Identifies the second barrier as preventing the next tile from overwriting data still in use.
Recognizes this is a shared-memory race-avoidance pattern, not host/device sync.

questions.question: In the tiled GEMM kernel, the outer loop advances with 'for (int t = 0; t < (N + TILE_SIZE - 1) / TILE_SIZE; t++)'. What does this loop iterate over? [ref_17]
choices: Tiles along the K (reduction) dimension, accumulating into a single scalar sum
Tiles along the output row dimension, writing one row per iteration
The batch dimension of the input matrices
The number of CUDA blocks launched
questions.correct_answer: Tiles along the K (reduction) dimension, accumulating into a single scalar sum
questions.reference_answer: The loop is commented "// Move along the K dimension tile by tile" [ref_17]. Each iteration loads one A tile and one B tile, does a TILE_SIZE-long dot-product accumulation into the thread's local sum, and the final sum is written to C after the loop.
scoring_points: Identifies the loop as walking the K / reduction dimension.
Notes the accumulation into a per-thread scalar sum.
Notes the result is written to C only after the loop completes.

questions.question: Why does the plain softmax sum exp(x_j) overflow for an input such as x = (1000, 1001, 1002)? [ref_15]
choices: Because exp(1000) is about 1.97e434, which exceeds the maximum representable float64 value of about 1.8e308
Because the input vector has more than two elements
Because the denominator is computed in integer arithmetic
Because softmax requires the inputs to be sorted first
questions.correct_answer: Because exp(1000) is about 1.97e434, which exceeds the maximum representable float64 value of about 1.8e308
questions.reference_answer: The course notes that the denominator sum exp(x_j) "may overflow" and gives exactly this example: exp(1000) is about 1.97e434 while max(float64) is about 1.8e308, so the exponential itself is not representable [ref_15].
scoring_points: Selects the overflow explanation with the numeric comparison.
Cites that exp(1000) ~ 1.97e434 exceeds max float64 ~ 1.8e308.
Recognizes the failure is in the exponentiation, before normalization.

questions.question: In the stable softmax derivation, the shift constant is chosen as c = m = max_j(x_j). Which statement best explains why this choice is made? [ref_13]
choices: It prevents overflow because exp(x_j - c) <= 1, and it avoids catastrophic underflow because the largest shifted term becomes exactly 0 in the exponent
It makes the output values sum to a value larger than one
It removes the need to divide by the denominator
It guarantees the output is exactly uniform
questions.correct_answer: It prevents overflow because exp(x_j - c) <= 1, and it avoids catastrophic underflow because the largest shifted term becomes exactly 0 in the exponent
questions.reference_answer: The course derives that to prevent overflow we need c >= max_j x_j - log Float_max, and then states: "To avoid catastrophic underflow: Choose c s.t. max(x_j - c) = 0", denoting the chosen c as m = max_j(x_j) [ref_13]. With this shift every exponent is <= 0, so no term overflows, and the largest term has exponent exactly 0 so it is not flushed to zero.
scoring_points: States that subtracting the max bounds all exponents at 0, preventing overflow.
States that the max term maps to exponent 0, avoiding catastrophic underflow.
Notes the normalization by the denominator is still required.

questions.question: In the online softmax recurrence, the normalizer is updated as d = d * expf(m - m_new) + expf(input[j] - m_new). What is the role of the factor expf(m - m_new)? [ref_8]
choices: It rescales the previously accumulated normalizer from the old maximum m to the new maximum m_new
It normalizes the final output to sum to one
It computes the running maximum itself
It is a numerical guard against division by zero
questions.correct_answer: It rescales the previously accumulated normalizer from the old maximum m to the new maximum m_new
questions.reference_answer: The course writes the update as d_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} e^{x_i - m_{j-1} + m_{j-1} - m_j} + e^{x_j - m_j} [ref_8]. The factor exp(m - m_new) is exactly the correction that re-bases the old partial sum, which was computed relative to m_{j-1}, onto the new maximum m_j, so the running normalizer stays consistent as the max grows.
scoring_points: Identifies the factor as a rescaling of the old accumulator to the new max.
Connects it to the m_{j-1} -> m_j change of reference point.
Notes the new element is added with the new max: exp(x_j - m_new).

questions.question: The course defines the online softmax state with m_{j-1} = max over 1<=i<=j-1 of x_i and d-hat_{j-1} = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} e^{x_i - m_{j-1}}. What is the key advantage of this formulation over the two-pass stable softmax? [ref_9]
choices: The maximum and the normalizer are updated together in a single streaming pass, so the input does not need to be read twice
It produces a different mathematical result from the two-pass version
It eliminates the need for any exponentiation
It requires storing the entire input vector in shared memory
questions.correct_answer: The maximum and the normalizer are updated together in a single streaming pass, so the input does not need to be read twice
questions.reference_answer: The course presents the online softmax as a recurrence whose input is (m_{j-1}, d-hat_{j-1}, x_j) and whose output is (m_j, d_j) [ref_9]. Because the running max and the running normalizer are carried forward together, one pass suffices; the two-pass stable softmax must first scan for the max and then scan again to accumulate the exponentials. The result is mathematically identical, only the traversal changes.
scoring_points: Identifies the single-pass / streaming advantage.
Notes that m and d are updated jointly as a recurrence.
Notes the result is mathematically equivalent to the two-pass version.
